newsitem.title: INDIA: Indian cotton prices weaken on tight money supply.
newsitem.headline: Indian cotton prices weaken on tight money supply.

text.p: Indian cotton prices weakened on Tuesday on tight money supply faced by millers, dealers said.
"Millers are facing stringent monetary conditions and low buying by them kept the market quiet," one dealer said.
In spot deals Bengal-deshi slid by five rupees at 775/805 rupees per maund (37.32 kg) while Punjab saw-ginned eased by 10 rupees at 1,400/1,630 rupees per maund.
Gujarat Kalyan (medium-staple) fell by 200 rupees to 11,100/11,300 rupees per candy (355.56 kg).
Dealers said the textile commissioner has convened a meeting of the Cotton Advisory Board on February 24 to access demand and supply position of cotton.
"The board may recommend more exports in view of sliding domestic prices," one dealer said.

They said while the board, at its last meeting two months ago, saw the cotton crop for the 1996/97 season at 15.50 million bales, traders are now putting the crop at an estimated 16-16.5 million bales.
Late rains in some of the producing centres have boosted crop prospects, dealers said.
